Fig. 2: Architecture of AVA-DINO. During training, the frozen DINOv3 visual encoder extracts multi-scale features from input images. Patch tokens are processed by dual-branch adapters (normal and anomaly pathways), while CLS tokens guide textbased routing via the frozen CLIP text encoder. Routing weights (wn, wa) dynamically combine adapted features to generate pixel-level anomaly maps and image-level predictions. During testing, the learned routing weights automatically steer features toward the appropriate pathway, producing anomaly maps and predictions on unseen images without further adaptation.

Fig. 1: Uniform adaptation transforms all samples identically through a single adapter, producing mixed features (top). Our dual adaptation routes feed embeddings f into specialized normal and anomaly adapters, providing 1) separated representations An(f), Aa(f) and 2) weights wn, wa to be fused together (bottom). Both the frameworks are shown at test time.
